subject: Request: custom KMS + 30d retention carveout for Lumen Health
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@lumenhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-03T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: KMS + retention ask for pilot

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team reviewed the pilot notes and asked whether Redwood can support customer-managed keys for the pilot dataset and also permit a 30-day ephemeral retention window for some audit logs tied to PHI dataset handling.

We need this documented as an exception request so our compliance team can move the pilot forward. Attached is a short intake form that lists the minimal controls they need.

Can you confirm whether a carve-out like this is feasible during a time-limited pilot, and what evidence you'd provide (audit logs, access reports, key rotation proof)?

Best,
Elena Torres
Head of InfoSec Programs
Lumen Health

[Attachment: lumen_byo_request_form.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-03T11:03:00-05:00
Subject: Fwd: KMS + retention ask for pilot

Grace / Karthik — forwarding Lumen's intake. They want customer-managed KMS + a 30-day limited retention for certain audit logs (PHI scope). Ben, flagging for security evidence.

Quick asks:
- Is there a safe path to support ephemeral retention for a single account (policy-level config)?
- If we expose BYOK for pilot, what minimum controls + artifacts can we promise (rotation timestamps, material lineage, audit-export)?

I think this qualifies as an "exception" rather than a product launch. Let's triage and give Elena a concrete set of options and an internal rollout plan.

Thanks,
Marissa
Product Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference

Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-04T08:27:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: KMS + retention ask for pilot

Thanks for the forward. Tagging Priyom for ops impact and runbook updates. My initial read: we can probably do a scoped exception if we treat it as a time-bound policy + off-path evidence export.

Proposed triage steps (for internal alignment):
1) Karthik: confirm infra feasibility for per-account retention override (30d) for select audit streams and any runtime risks for batch/kv cache. Estimate: can we isolate audit stream with separate retention TTL without major infra changes?
2) Ben: list minimal evidence artifacts we can provide (full audit stream export, key usage ledger, rotation timestamps, access log slice). Any compliance red flags for PHI?
3) Priyom: if we do an exception, what's the deployment + rollback runbook? Who owns gate checks and sign-offs?
4) Marissa: I'll draft a short customer-facing option matrix (3 options: 1) standard Redwood retention + managed keys; 2) scoped BYOK + 30d audit retention exception; 3) limited POC with synthetic subset) and share next steps.

Can team respond with short bullets by EOD tomorrow so I can push a recommended option to Lumen by Friday?

Grace
Sr. Product Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

--
On Wed, Nov 3, 2027 at 11:03 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Grace / Karthik — forwarding Lumen's intake...

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-05T13:40:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Re: Fwd: KMS + retention ask for pilot

High level from infra: we can implement a per-account retention override for select audit topics by adding a retention TTL flag to the audit-routing layer and a separate cold-storage lifecycle rule. Implementation estimate: 2 sprints (4 weeks) to build, 1 week to QA and bake runbooks. Short-term alternate: we can support an export-based workaround — stream the relevant audit topic to a customer-owned S3 (requires routing + an export job) and then they control retention. That path needs access/consent gating.

Risks:
- Mixing PHI audit slices with global aggregation pipelines could complicate observability and incite extra SRE throttling keys.
- BYOK: we have the code paths for customer-managed keys in dedicated deployments; for hosted pilot we'd need a short-term enclave flow (customer key material never leaves their KMS; we store a key reference). That is doable but requires security sign-off and updated terms.

I'll put a short RFC/estimate in the shared doc.

Karthik
Engineering Lead, Runtime
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: retention_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-05T16:22:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Re: Fwd: KMS + retention ask for pilot

Short security input:
- Evidence we can provide for a BYOK + 30d audit retention exception:
  * Exported audit slice (signed manifest) covering RPC headers, request IDs, timestamps (we can redact payloads containing PHI)
  * KMS key usage ledger (who invoked key, timestamps, abbreviated key id)
  * Rotation proof: metadata showing rotation events (timestamps + rotating key id), not key material
  * Access report: SRE/service accounts that accessed the export pipeline during the window

Compliance concern: we'll need a written, time-boxed exception with approvals from both Redwood Security and Lumen's compliance lead. For PHI, confirm whether their legal team requires a BAA amendment. If yes, procurement/finance needs to be looped.

I'll draft the evidence checklist and a short security sign-off template we can send to Lumen.

Ben Carter
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: soc2_scoped_items.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-07T17:40:00-05:00
Subject: Re: KMS + retention ask for pilot — proposed options and next steps

Elena — thanks for the request and for sending the intake form. We reviewed internally and propose three options for the pilot (summarized below). Please tell us which you prefer and we will produce a short exception agreement + evidence pack.

Option A — Standard hosted configuration (fastest)
- Redwood-managed keys, standard audit retention (180d)
- Evidence: full audit export for the pilot period (redacted)
- Timeline: immediate onboarding

Option B — Scoped BYOK + 30d audit retention exception (recommended for PHI limited pilot)
- Customer-managed KMS reference (BYOK reference token) for pilot tenant in hosted environment
- Per-account retention override for selected audit topics set to 30 days; we will export a signed audit slice to Lumen's S3 nightly for durability (Lumen controls final deletion)
- Evidence: audit slice export (signed manifest), key usage ledger, rotation metadata, access report
- Requirements: written exception + security sign-off + confirmation on BAA scope; estimate 4 weeks to enable in pilot path; can be time-boxed to 90 days operationally

Option C — Synthetic subset POC (least risk)
- Move PHI-representative (synthetic) data into pilot; use Redwood-managed keys and standard retention
- Evidence: synthetic dataset audit + export; fastest to start

Next steps: pick an option by EOD Friday, 2027-11-12. If Option B, we'll generate an exception template and Ben will lead the security sign-off; Karthik will open the infra RFC and provide a firm plan and rollout timeline. Priyom will own the runbook and rollback steps.

I've attached a retention matrix and the intake form we received. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call this week to walk through options with your compliance folks.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Product Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: retention_matrix.xlsx]
[Attachment: lumen_byo_request_form.pdf]
